task.title: Migrate database pool to PgBouncer
task.objective: Resolve connection starvation under burst traffic by introducing PgBouncer transaction-mode pooling
task.notes: Pool exhaustion reproduced with k6 load test (500 VUs). Setting up pool sizing benchmarks.

findings.statement: Postgres direct connections peak at 100 max_connections, resulting in FATAL: 53300
Prepared statements require special handling in PgBouncer transaction mode

attempts.description: Increased max_connections to 300 on Postgres server
attempts.outcome: Exhausted RAM on test instance leading to OOM killer invoking
attempts.errorDetails: Out of memory: Killed process postgres

attempts.description: Deployed PgBouncer container in transaction mode with pool_size 25
attempts.outcome: Throughput increased by 4x without memory spike; connection errors dropped to 0

decisions.decision: Use PgBouncer transaction pooling instead of increasing PostgreSQL server max_connections
decisions.rationale: Keeps database server RAM usage bounded while sustaining 10,000 requests/sec

openQuestions.question: Does our query builder use named prepared statements that fail under transaction pooling?

nextSteps.step: Audit ORM query configuration for server-side prepared statements
Deploy PgBouncer configuration to staging environment
